gk_notebook.d: The goalkeeping coach hands you a file with every penalty taken by every striker in the league over three years.

o.r: By March you know where half the league shoots. Less sleep, but you don’t shake on the spot.
The notebook stays in the locker. You work on reflexes and keep your head light.

gk_sweeper.d: The new coach wants a keeper who plays with his feet, sweeps up to thirty metres out and starts attacks.

o.r: For a few months back-passes make you sweat. Then team-mates start looking for you.
You keep saving the way you know. The coach notes the refusal and looks at you differently.

gk_howler.d: A tame shot slips under your body. The clip circulates for a week. From that day you train your handling with a new anger.

gk_second.d: Ahead of you is a thirty-four-year-old keeper who never makes a mistake. The coach says your time will come.

o.r: You watch him train every morning. You play little, but you understand why he never errs.
The director nods: at the end of the season there will be a club where you play.

o.rw: You save everything in every practice match. In November the coach changes his mind.
o.rl: The veteran doesn’t crack under pressure. Meanwhile you’ve made enemies in the dressing room.

gk_crosses.d: The team conceded five goals from crosses in a month. Everyone is looking at you.

o.r: Hours jumping among six team-mates shoving you. Shoulders ache, hands find the ball.
You become the one who shouts. The marking sorts itself out and the coach approves.

gk_kicking.d: A former American football punter offers private sessions on long kicks.

o.r: Your goal kicks now reach the opposition’s final third. The strikers thank you.
You prefer sessions a metre from the ball machine.

gk_armband.d: The captain leaves in January. The players vote: they want you.

o.r: A captain in goal talks to the referee from far away. You learn to make yourself heard.
You’d rather think about your posts. Nobody holds it against you.

gk_rival_signing.d: The club buys a keeper who starts for his national team. Officially, “for competition”.

o.l: Win the place on the pitch
o.rw: Decisive saves in the first three games. The new arrival sits on the bench.
o.rl: He starts better, you concede a soft goal. The bench becomes your home.

o.r: Your agent starts making calls. The club doesn’t take it well.
Cups for you, league for him. You play less and arrive fresh.

gk_eyes.d: The doctor finds a slight defect in your sight. With contact lenses the first weeks feel odd, then the ball arrives sharper than ever.

gk_shootout.d: Quarter-final, it goes to penalties. You have one minute before the first kick.

o.r: You remember three takers out of five. You save one and they all look at you differently.

o.rw: You dance on the line and smile. Two of them miss. The clip of your faces goes viral.
o.rl: The first one sends you the wrong way and winks. The away fans can’t stop laughing.

gk_mentor.d: An eighteen-year-old keeper comes up from the youth team. Everyone says he’ll take your place.

o.r: You show him how to read a taker from his run-up. You’ll leave him a few games, and that’s fair.
The place is still yours. The dressing room notices the coldness.

gk_ageing_reflexes.d: The coach’s data is clear: your reflexes are a tenth slower than three years ago.

o.r: You position yourself half a metre earlier. Fewer spectacular saves, but no more goals conceded.
You win the tenth back. Your back, however, starts to complain.

dc_markstar.d: On Sunday the league’s top scorer comes to town. The coach asks how you want to stop him.

o.rw: He doesn’t touch the ball for ninety minutes. At full time he asks for your shirt.
o.rl: He drags you out of the box and a team-mate scores in the space you left.

o.r: You pass him around. He scores only from a penalty, and the coach is happy anyway.

dc_buildup.d: The new manager bans long balls: the centre-back has to build play.

o.r: Two dangerous turnovers in September, then the forward pass becomes your trademark.
You keep clearing it. No mistakes, but there’s less and less room for you in the new system.

dc_setpieces.d: The club hires a coach just for corners and free kicks. He wants a defender to attack the near post.

o.r: Headers after every session. A few goals will come.
Someone has to stay back: you learn to read counter-attacks.

dc_redcard.d: Last man, a foul from behind in the twentieth minute. A three-match ban and a week of front pages.

dc_partner.d: An experienced centre-back arrives next to you. Someone has to command the line.

o.r: You call offside and push the line up. He lets you and covers your back.
You listen and mark. You learn more in six months than in three years.

dc_gym.d: The fitness coach offers two summer programmes.

o.r: You add four kilos of muscle. Nobody moves you in duels.
Yoga, bands, sleep. Your body thanks you and will for years.

dc_fullback.d: Three full-backs injured. The coach asks you to play right-back for two months.

o.r: You suffer against quick wingers, but you play every game. The coach won’t forget.
You stay a centre-back, on the bench. It doesn’t go unnoticed.

dc_armband.d: The coach calls you into his office with the armband in his hand.

o.r: From today, the hard press conferences are yours.
The armband goes to someone else. You keep leading the defence without a title.

dc_slower.d: Over thirty metres you now lose to everyone.

o.r: You read the play instead of chasing it. Experience instead of legs.
In the middle of three you don’t need to run: you need to think and pass.

dc_viral_tackle.d: A sliding clearance on the line in the ninetieth minute. The clip goes around the world with epic music.

tz_overlap.d: The coach wants you on the byline in every attack.

o.l: Up and down for ninety minutes
o.r: Cross after cross. You can’t feel your legs at full time, but the team creates more.
Someone has to watch the back. Nobody gets past on your side.

tz_otherside.d: A full-back is needed on the other side. You’d have to go to the byline on your weak foot.

o.rw: You cut onto your strong foot and find spaces nobody expects.
o.rl: Every cross hits the first defender. You’re back on your side by February.

o.r: Someone else takes the place. You wait your turn.

tz_winger.d: In a friendly you play as a winger and make two assists. The coach wants to try it again.

o.r: More dribbling, more shots. When you go back to full-back, you attack like a winger.
You thank him and go back to working on tackles.

tz_altitude.d: The club organises two weeks at two thousand metres for anyone who wants.

o.r: You’re breathless for the first days. In September you outrun everyone.
You come back rested and calm. Your stamina is what it was.

tz_crosscoach.d: The assistant coach suggests specific crossing work after training.

o.r: By December the ball always finds the right head.
You’d rather reach the byline first than deliver the ball better.

tz_nightmare.d: A nineteen-year-old winger beats you six times in one half on national TV. You rewatch it until dawn.

tz_inverted.d: The coach wants you to move into midfield next to the holding player when in possession.

o.r: You see the pitch from another angle. The coach considers you indispensable.
The classic game on the flank stays yours: crosses and overlaps.

tz_losing_pace.t: The sprint isn’t what it was
tz_losing_pace.d: Young wingers get half a step ahead of you.

o.r: You show them wide and close them down earlier. Less running, fewer mistakes.
You win something back. Past thirty, the muscles protest.

tz_chant.d: The fans invent a chant about your runs down the flank. They sing it even when you lose the ball.

med_screen.d: The coach draws a line on the board: your job ends there.

o.r: You win the ball and give it to the nearest man. The defenders love you.

o.rw: A couple of well-timed runs and the coach turns a blind eye.
o.rl: A counter-attack comes through the gap you left. The board comes out again.

med_diagonals.d: You watch the great playmakers and notice the thirty-metre ball to the far flank.

o.r: By spring the ball crosses the pitch and lands on the right foot.
Two touches, always short. You never lose the ball and the coach knows it.

med_suspension.d: One booking from a ban, you go in late in the ninetieth minute of a game already won. You miss the big match.

med_enforcer.d: Their playmaker scored twice against you last time. In the dressing room someone says to “let him feel the first tackle”.

o.l: Go in hard on the first ball
o.rw: A yellow, but he vanishes from the game. You win.
o.rl: Straight red in the tenth minute. You lose and the coach doesn’t speak to you for a week.

o.r: You take away his passing lanes rather than his ankles. He barely touches the ball.

med_regista.d: The new coach sees a deep-lying playmaker in you. You’ve always been the destroyer.

o.r: Fewer tackles, more passes. You discover you see the pitch better than you thought.
The shield in front of the defence remains your job.

med_engine.d: The holding midfielder runs the most. The fitness coach offers double loads.

o.r: Twelve kilometres a game. Now and then your body sends a warning.
Cryotherapy, sleep, diet. You run as before, without the risk.

med_armband.d: In the dressing room everyone talks to you before they talk to the coach. The armband seems a formality.

o.r: You officially become what you already were.
You lead anyway, without the title or the pressure.

med_heavy_legs.d: After three games in eight days you struggle to get out of bed.

o.r: You play the games that matter and rest the others. Your head works for your legs.
The coach appreciates it. Your body holds, for now.

med_pundit.d: A pundit calls you that in prime time. You print the quote and stick it in your locker.

mez_runs.d: On video the coach notices you always arrive in the box a second late.

o.r: Once you learn the run, the ball starts reaching you ten metres from goal.
You are the last pass, not the last touch.

mez_freekicks.d: The usual taker leaves. Free kicks around the box are up for grabs.

o.rw: The first one goes in the top corner. From that day the ball is yours.
o.rl: Three into the stands. The captain takes the ball out of your hands.

o.r: You focus on the rest of the game.

mez_street.d: In summer your friends play five-a-side on concrete every evening.

o.r: On concrete you keep the ball close. You come back with a new trick.
You watch whole games and draw the movements. You understand where space opens.

mez_press.d: The new coach wants his central midfielders to press the ball carrier up to the opposition box.

o.r: You run like never before and win the ball high. You shoot less.
You stay the creative one. The coach huffs every time you don’t track back.

mez_number10.d: The club’s historic playmaker retires. The kit man asks if you want his number.

o.r: That number is heavy on your back. It makes you play with your head up.
The number you arrived with brings you luck.

mez_screamer.d: A volley from outside the box flies in under the bar. The league shortlists it for goal of the year.

mez_rival.d: A team-mate who plays your position mocks you in the group chat.

o.rw: You dominate him for a month. The starting place becomes yours.
o.rl: The tension turns into a scuffle. The coach picks him, at least he doesn’t fight.

o.r: He appreciates the maturity. The team-mate keeps laughing, but quietly.

mez_tempo.d: An old coach tells you great midfielders don’t run more: they decide when to run.

o.r: One touch more when needed, one less when possible. The team breathes with you.
Your football is intensity. You just need to get there before the others.

mez_deeper.d: The coach suggests dropping in front of the defence to prolong your career.

o.r: Less running, more thinking. The pitch looks bigger to you.
Still up and down, as long as your body holds.

ala_1v1.d: “When you have the ball, go at the full-back. Always,” says the youth coach.

o.rw: You beat your man and deliver golden balls into the box.
o.rl: You lose thirty balls a game. The first-team coach disagrees with the youth coach.

o.r: Dribble when needed, pass when better. You play more often.

ala_weakfoot.d: Everyone knows you cut onto your strong foot. Full-backs wait for you there.

o.l: A year on the other foot
o.r: Clumsy months, then full-backs no longer know which way to show you.
Everyone knows where you’re going. Nobody can stop you anyway.

ala_cutinside.d: The coach wants to switch you to the other flank so you can cut in and shoot.

o.r: The curler into the far corner becomes your signature.
Crosses from the byline, like the old wingers. The strikers are grateful.

ala_sprint.d: A former Olympic sprinter offers to work on your acceleration.

o.r: You gain a metre in the first five. Your muscles hold, for now.
You’d rather have a quiet summer.

ala_showboat.d: Ninetieth minute, four-nil up. You have the ball and the fans want something special.

o.r: The stadium goes wild. Their full-back doesn’t, and neither does your coach.
No show. The coach pats you on the shoulder.

ala_hamstring.d: A cold sprint in the warm-up and you feel a pull behind your thigh. Nothing torn, but the muscle stays fragile.

ala_nickname.d: A commentator calls you “the lightning” and it sticks. Since then it arrives at every stadium before you.

ala_trackback.d: Against big teams the coach wants you to become a wing-back.

o.r: You run twice as much and score less, but you’re never subbed off.
You wait for the counter. When it doesn’t come, the coach glares at you.

ala_socials.d: A clothing brand offers money for weekly trick videos.

o.r: Millions of views. You skip a few sessions for filming.
You stay focused. The coach doesn’t say it, but he notices.

ala_central.d: Your acceleration has dropped. The coach sees you as a number ten.

o.r: Fewer metres, more ideas. The ball always goes through you.
More sprints down the line, while your legs allow.

pun_shots.d: The club’s old centre-forward, now a coach, offers you his recipe.

o.r: Right, left, volleys. Your foot goes cold in front of the keeper.
You learn to vanish from defenders’ sight and reappear at the far post.

pun_penalties.d: The regular taker is suspended. Ninetieth minute, nil-nil, the referee points to the spot.

o.rw: Keeper one way, ball the other. Penalties are yours now.
o.rl: Off the post. You’ll carry the stadium’s silence for weeks.

o.r: No risk, no glory.

pun_target.d: The team plays long balls. The coach wants you to battle and hold the ball with your back to goal.

o.r: Gym and headers. You become the reference point the team needed.
You stay technical and mobile. The coach looks for a big man on the market.

pun_drought.d: Every shot hits a post, a keeper or a defender. The more you think, the heavier the ball gets.

pun_supersub.d: The coach says you’re perfect for the last twenty minutes, when defences are tired.

o.r: You come on and score. You play little, but you matter.

o.rw: Two braces as a starter and the argument ends.
o.rl: The coach doesn’t budge and leaves you out out of spite.

pun_star_arrives.d: The club spends a fortune on a famous centre-forward. In your position.

o.rw: You outscore him in the first half of the season. You play together.
o.rl: He starts and doesn’t stop. You watch from the bench.

o.r: Your agent opens talks.
You drift wide, make room for him, feed him assists. Another career inside yours.

pun_presser.d: At a press conference a journalist asks if you’re overrated.

o.r: You smile and leave. Next Sunday you score and don’t celebrate.
The quote is on every website. The club asks you to tone it down.

pun_gym.d: The nutritionist asks what kind of striker you want to be in two years.

o.r: You hold defenders off with one arm. You lose something in the sprint.
Three kilos less, a step quicker over the first metre.

pun_bicycle.d: A high cross, your back to goal, you throw yourself. The goal ends up in the Sunday show’s opening titles.

pun_false9.d: The new coach wants a striker who drops deep and leaves space for runners.

o.r: You touch more balls than ever. Others score, but it starts with you.
The box is home. No system moves you out of it.

pun_poacher_late.d: Modern pressing costs you energy. The coach lets you choose.

o.r: You don’t press anyone any more. But in the box you always get there first.
The team appreciates the sacrifice. Your body a bit less.

y_school.d: Exams fall in the week of the youth final. You can’t be in both places.

o.r: You pass. The coach says nothing, but your family is proud.
You score the winner. The headmaster glares at you for a year.
No sleep, exam passed, final played half asleep. You manage, and you pay for it.

y_agent.d: Two men offer to manage your career. One drives a car worth as much as the stadium.

o.r: He takes you everywhere and talks to everyone. About you, like a product.
He’s known your father for thirty years. He’ll never sell you to the highest bidder.
You manage yourself. It takes longer, but you’ve read what you sign.

y_contract.d: {club} offer you five years. Your agent suggests a short deal.

o.r: The club sees you as an investment and plays you.
You stay free to leave. The club knows, and treats you accordingly.

y_u17.d: The youth national team calls you up for a two-week tournament mid-season.

o.r: You play against the best of your age. You come back tired and more confident.
The coach gives you a cup debut. One opportunity chases another.

y_idol.d: At a charity evening you find yourself next to {idol}. You have thirty seconds.

o.r: He explains the detail that made him unique. You’ll carry it forever.
The photo goes round the whole country. Your mother frames it.

y_homesick.d: Far from home, at {club}, the evenings never end.

o.r: The smile returns. The coach notices a few sessions missed for flights.
You bury yourself in work. You get stronger, and a bit lonelier.

y_party.d: Team-mates throw a party. The game is Sunday at three.

o.rw: Two hours, a soft drink, in bed by midnight. Nobody notices.
o.rl: A photo hits social media at four in the morning. The coach sees it before you do.

o.r: On Sunday you’re the sharpest player on the pitch.

y_growth.d: Eight centimetres in a year. Your knees ache and your coordination needs finding again.

y_shaved.d: After your first session with the first team the veterans shave your head. It’s their way of saying welcome.

y_friend.d: You grew up together. Now you’re fighting for the same first-team place.

o.r: You train together and push each other. The place stays open.
You win every duel. The friendship doesn’t survive the season.

y_diet.d: No sugar, no fried food, weigh-in every Monday.

o.r: Your body changes in two months. You miss Friday pizza.
You’re happy. Monday’s scales a bit less.

y_languages.d: The club offers evening English and Spanish classes.

o.r: Two languages in two years. One day you’ll need them in another dressing room.
You spend the evenings watching games.

y_trial.d: A big club invites you for a week’s trial. Your club advises against it.

o.rw: They write your name in red in their notebook. In June they’ll call.
o.rl: Your legs shake for seven days. You go home with a free shirt and nothing else.

o.r: The club values your loyalty and promises you playing time.

y_loan.d: The coach is honest: this year you’d play little. He suggests a loan at the end of the season.

o.r: In June a club will come where you play every Sunday.

o.rw: You train like a madman and start by January.
o.rl: You stay at the bottom of the pecking order all year.

y_knee.d: A twist in training, an MRI, three days of waiting. No ligament damage, but the fear stays.

y_haters.d: After a bad game you read the comments under your photo. You shouldn’t have.

y_nerves.d: Before big games you can’t eat.

o.r: You learn to breathe and put your thoughts in order. The knot loosens.

o.rw: It goes the way it came. Maybe it was just age.
o.rl: The knot becomes a block. You play two games like a ghost.

y_diploma.d: You have one year left. Night school ends at ten.

o.r: Tired, but with the diploma in your pocket. A plan B never hurts.
Football is your plan A, B and C.

p_renewal.d: {club} offer a new deal with a loyalty clause.

o.r: You become one of the pillars of the project.
The market notices you’re available.

p_rival_offer.d: Your club’s historic rivals offer double your salary. The news is in the papers.

o.r: The fans unfurl a banner against you. The offers, though, increase.
You kiss the badge after your next goal. The fans won’t forget it.

p_captain.d: The dressing room votes. Your name comes up more than any other.

o.r: As captain you speak for everyone. Even when things go badly.
The armband goes to someone else. Your weight in the dressing room remains.

p_coach_clash.d: Your mistake costs the game. The coach drops you for three matches and says so at the press conference.

o.rw: The dressing room sides with you. In March the coach is sacked.
o.rl: The club sides with the coach. A long winter begins for you.

o.r: You’re back in the side after three games. Stronger and without a row.

p_wedding.d: The date is set mid-season. The honeymoon is a problem.

o.r: Married on Saturday, on the pitch on Wednesday.
Ten days of sun. You come back happy and two kilos heavier.

p_baby.d: You sleep three hours a night and have never been happier. The next Sunday you walk out with your child’s name written on your wrist.

p_foundation.d: In the neighbourhood where you grew up, the local pitch is about to close.

o.r: The pitch reopens with your name on the gate. Your days get fuller.
Nobody knows. You do.

p_boots.d: A sportswear brand wants to design a boot with your name on it.

o.rw: You see them on kids’ feet at the local pitch. Nothing better.
o.rl: The new model gives you blisters for a month.

o.r: Never change a winning team. Or boots.

p_ballon_hype.d: The papers put you among the favourites. They ask what you think.

o.rw: The pressure fires you up. You play the best season of your life.
o.rl: Every game becomes an exam. The pressure crushes you.

o.r: You lower the spotlight and raise your level in training.

p_saga.d: For three months every paper has sold you to a different club. The president won’t let you go.

o.r: You skip a training session. The message is clear to everyone, and it costs.
You shut the door on the market. The fans appreciate it, you a bit less.

p_injection.d: A muscle strain on the eve of the biggest game of the year. The doctor can give you an injection.

o.rw: Ninety minutes without feeling a thing. You win.
o.rl: In the twentieth minute you feel it tear. You’ll be out for about two months.

o.r: You watch from the stands. The muscle heals, the coach is disappointed.

p_revolution.d: A young coach arrives with radical ideas: drone training, video every day.

o.r: It takes time to understand. Then you discover things about yourself you didn’t know.
The old way worked. The coach notes who is pulling the other way.

p_fight.d: One tackle too many in a practice game, two shoves, a slap. Fines for both and the photo in the papers.

p_chant.d: The fans dedicate a chant to you. You hear it start while you warm up and get goosebumps.

p_mentor.d: A sixteen-year-old follows you everywhere in training asking a thousand questions.

o.r: You teach him the details nobody teaches. It makes you feel useful.
You have your own goals. The kid finds another teacher.

p_media.d: The press office suggests a course for interviews.

o.r: Your interviews become quotes. Journalists seek you out.
Authentic, sometimes too much.

p_ritual.d: You’ve won three games in a row wearing the same socks. The kit man wants to wash them.

o.r: Same socks, same order in the dressing room, same foot onto the pitch. It works, until it doesn’t.
Clean socks. You win with your legs.

p_hot.d: Six games in a row among the best on the pitch. Everything you touch works.

p_anxiety.d: You can’t sleep, your heart races for no reason. Nobody at the club has noticed.

o.r: Talking about it is the hardest save. After a month you breathe again.

o.rw: It passes with the holidays.
o.rl: It explodes in February. The second half of the season is a wall.

p_tv.d: A sports show wants you as a regular Monday-night guest.

o.r: Viewers love you. The coach less so, when you arrive tired on Tuesday.
Monday is for recovery.

p_derby.d: Decisive in the derby. For a week every café in town offers you a coffee.

p_fake_news.d: A website claims you fell out with the coach and want to leave. It’s false, but the denial comes late.

v_exotic.d: A Gulf club and an American club offer unprecedented sums.

o.r: Sun, money and less pressure. At the end of the season a concrete offer will come.
While your legs hold, you stay where teams play to win.

v_rotation.d: The coach suggests you play every other game.

o.r: You play less but better. Your body is grateful.

o.l: You want to play them all
o.rw: You prove you’re still there. Nobody mentions age any more.
o.rl: By November you’re running on empty. The coach was right.

v_badges.d: The federation opens a course for active players.

o.r: Monday lessons make you watch games with new eyes.
There’s still playing to do.

v_physio.d: Many veterans pay for a personal physio and cryotherapy at home.

o.r: Two hours a day of body care. You feel twenty-five again, almost.
You’ve always done it this way and it went fine.

v_revolt.d: Late wages, terrible results. The young players want to strike.

o.r: You talk to the board and the lads. Everyone goes back to playing.
Everything stays unresolved, and someone accuses you of only thinking about yourself.

v_testimonial.d: The club organises an evening to celebrate your years in the shirt. The stadium is full.

v_replacement.d: The club unveils a twenty-year-old in your position. At the press conference they call him “the future”.

v_finished.d: A newspaper headline says you’re in decline. You cut out the article: it’ll be fuel.

v_business.d: A friend suggests opening a restaurant together.

o.r: It does well. Some nights you stay out later than you should.
For now your head stays on the pitch.

v_family_home.t: Your family wants to go home
v_family_home.d: The kids are growing up far from their grandparents. Back home they ask when you’ll return.

o.l: Look for a club at home
o.r: At the end of the season your agent will only listen to offers from your country.
The family accepts, but the subject will come back.

v_last_push.t: One last trophy with the club
v_last_push.d: To give everything to the club, they suggest you quit the national team.

o.r: A summer of rest. You reach May with fresh legs.
Club and country. The calendar shows no mercy.

v_armband_pass.d: The team’s young leader is ready to be captain.

o.r: You put it on his arm in front of everyone. A gesture the dressing room will remember.
You earned it. Some people grumble, though.

e_one_more_year.d: {club} offer you a one-year deal, lower wages and a mentoring role.

o.r: You play less and teach more. It’s still football.
You want to play every Sunday. In June your agent will look further down.
You say it at the press conference. From now, every game is a goodbye.

e_farewell_tour.d: In every stadium, even hostile ones, applause starts as you come on.

e_player_coach.d: The coach asks you to be his assistant while still playing when needed.

o.r: Half the time on the pitch, half on the touchline. You’re already preparing for afterwards.
While there’s playing, you play.

e_body_stop.d: Your Achilles hurts every morning. The doctor talks about wear, not injury.

e_hometown.d: The club where you started as a boy writes: they’d like to close your career together.

o.r: At the end of the season their offer will arrive.
You’ll close the circle another way.

e_documentary.d: A streaming platform wants to film a documentary about your last season.

o.r: They follow you everywhere. The trailer moves half the country.
You want to live your last season without narrating it.

e_last_derby.d: When you’re subbed off in the seventieth minute, even the rival fans stand.

e_academy_job.d: The club offers you the U17 team when you stop.

o.r: You already know what you’ll do the day after your last game.
The future can wait a little longer.

e_record.d: You’re a few games away from the club appearance record.

o.r: You play even when tired. The record becomes an obsession.
If it comes, it comes without forcing it.

e_tv_career.d: A TV channel offers you a commentator contract for when you retire.

o.r: The microphone awaits. Meanwhile you study games with a new eye.
Your future is in the dugout, not the studio.

e_letter.d: You feel the need to thank the people who followed you for twenty years.

o.r: Thousands of replies. Someone sends a photo of your first autograph.
A lap of honour after the game is worth a thousand words.

n_callup.d: The phone rings at eight in the morning: the {nation} head coach has put you in the squad.

o.r: The post in the national shirt becomes the most viewed of your life.
You arrive at the camp in silence. The senior players appreciate it.

n_debut.d: Packed stadium, anthem, and this time you start. The coach says: “Play like you do for your club.”

o.rw: Your best move sets up the goal. The coach hugs you when you come off.
o.rl: Two balls lost in the first ten minutes. You’re off at half-time.

o.r: No mistakes, no headlines. The door stays open.

n_system.t: Out of position for your country
n_system.d: The national coach plays you in a position you’ve never played for your club.

o.r: You don’t shine, but the coach knows he can count on you.
You tell journalists. At the next call-up your name is missing.

n_captain.d: The long-time captain retires from international football. The coach wants to give you the armband.

o.r: You sing the anthem in front of everyone, armband on. Another weight, another honour.
The coach values your humility and makes you vice-captain.

n_prep.t: The summer of the big tournament
n_prep.d: After the season comes the big tournament with the national team. Your club would like to manage your load.

o.r: You arrive at the camp in perfect shape, a little tired.
A few games missed, fresh legs for the summer.

n_friendlies.d: Your club asks you to skip the March friendlies to rest.

o.r: The club is grateful. The national coach less so.
Two intercontinental flights in a week. The coach notices.

n_provocation.d: The opposing national team’s star says your side “scares nobody”.

o.rw: You win and your reply becomes a slogan.
o.rl: You lose, and your words come back to haunt you for weeks.

o.r: The pitch will talk. The coach likes your calm.

n_anthem.d: The cameras catch you singing the anthem with your eyes closed. The image becomes the cover of the game.

n_dropped.d: You read the squad list on TV. Your name isn’t there, and nobody called you.

n_retire.d: You have {caps} caps for {nation}. Your body is asking you to choose.

o.r: A letter to the fans and one last game. Your club gets a fresher player back.
While the coach calls, you answer.

n_shootout.d: In the knockout stage it goes to penalties. The coach asks who wants to take one.

o.rw: You score yours. The whole country knows your name.
o.rl: You miss. The photo of your head in your hands is on every front page.

o.r: You watch from the centre circle, arm in arm with team-mates.

n_gk_shootout.d: Extra time is over. It’s you against five of the opposing nation’s takers.

o.r: You read two of them. The rest is fate, but you prepared.

o.rw: Two misses. Your faces become legend.
o.rl: They score them all. The dancing just looks silly.

n_new_gen.d: Three twenty-year-olds are pushing for your place in the national team.

o.r: You become the group’s senior figure. The coach wants you for your experience.

o.rw: You win your place back with performances.
o.rl: The kids are quicker. The coach takes note.

n_blame.d: A heavy defeat and the fans blame you. The coach defends you, half-heartedly.

n_milestone.d: The federation presents you with a commemorative shirt before the game. The stadium applauds.

i_car.d: A car hits you from behind on the ring road. Whiplash and ten days in a neck brace.

i_flu.d: A thirty-nine-degree fever for a week. Half the squad catches it after you.

i_sacked.d: The coach is sacked. With the new one, everyone starts from zero.

i_takeover.d: A foreign fund buys the club and brings in three signings in January. The team is stronger.

i_wages.d: The club hasn’t paid for three months. Your agent says it’s time to look around at the end of the season.

i_potm.d: The league names you player of the month. The trophy ends up on your mother’s shelf.

i_bad_company.d: A team-mate drags you into nights that end too late. You notice when your legs don’t turn.

i_family.d: A family member is ill. The club lets you go without asking questions, and you won’t forget it.

i_var.d: A goal of yours is ruled out by VAR by a centimetre. It’s debated for days.

i_heat.d: Pre-season camp is somewhere forty degrees hot. Two weeks of toil without a ball.

i_kit.d: The club picks you to launch the new shirt. Your name is the best-seller.

i_meme.d: Your face after a miss becomes a worldwide meme. You laugh too.

i_dog.d: You adopt a dog. Walks before bed clear your head better than any session.

i_travel.d: Flight cancelled, twelve hours at the airport before the cup game. You play anyway.

i_teammate_hurt.d: In training one of your tackles injures a team-mate. He’s out for a month. He forgives you, you less so.

i_new_stadium.d: The new stadium opens. The first game in the new home tastes different.

x_gk_video.d: The match analyst cuts together every goal you conceded last year, one after another. Forty minutes.

o.l: Watch them all, again and again
o.r: You find that on one shot in three you were half a step out of position. Not any more.
You need confidence, not a trial. You go back out with warm hands.

x_gk_gloves.d: Your kit sponsor wants you in the new model, lighter and more photogenic. You know your old pair by heart.

o.r: They look great in photos. In the rain the ball slips a little more.
The sponsor frowns. Your grip stays what it always was.

x_gk_long_throw.d: The team has very fast forwards. The coach asks you to throw it out immediately, before the opposition resets.

o.r: Two or three breaks a game start from your hands. Some end in goals.
You slow it down and let team-mates push up. Fewer chances, fewer risks.

x_gk_penalty_taker.d: Last minute of a game already won, penalty to you. Team-mates wave you forward to take it.

o.rw: Ball one way, keeper the other. You celebrate running back to your empty goal.
o.rl: Over the bar. The stadium laughs, the coach doesn’t.

o.r: Your job is at the other end. The usual taker steps up.

x_gk_back_injury.d: Every high claim leaves a twinge in your lower back. The physio suggests limiting diving in training.

o.r: You protect your back. On high balls you’re a touch less explosive.

o.rw: The twinge fades on its own. You keep claiming every cross.
o.rl: In November your back locks. Two months out.

x_gk_keeper_coach.d: A new goalkeeping coach arrives with methods opposite to the last one: lots of reaction work, hardly any claiming.

o.r: Weeks of tennis balls and reflexes. Your spring becomes a weapon.

o.l: Ask to work on claiming too
o.r: You find a compromise. Better claiming, better positioning.

x_dc_captain_voice.t: The line that won’t step up
x_dc_captain_voice.d: The back line always sits too deep and opponents shoot from distance unchallenged. Someone has to raise their voice.

o.r: Team-mates hate you for a week. Then the line steps up on its own.
Your striker doesn’t touch the ball. The rest isn’t up to you.

x_dc_left_foot.d: The team needs a left-sided centre-back and you’re right-footed. The coach asks you to learn to build with your left.

o.r: A few balls lost at first. By spring you open play with both feet.
You know your spot. You keep winning tackles.

x_dc_striker_emergency.d: A goal down, no strikers on the bench. The coach sends you up front for the high balls.

o.rw: In the ninetieth minute you head it in. Your first goal as a striker.
o.rl: You win every duel, but the ball won’t go in.

o.r: You’d rather keep the defence organised. The coach sighs.

x_dc_duel_king.d: You struggle against big strikers. The assistant coach says: get stronger, or get to the ball first.

o.r: Months of contact in training. Now the strikers bounce off you.
You study movement and move a moment earlier. Contact becomes unnecessary.

x_dc_own_goal.d: A harmless cross, a clumsy touch, the ball in your own net. The team loses by a goal. Nobody blames you, but you can’t sleep.

x_dc_back_three.d: The team switches to a back three. You get the wide role: defend and support the attack down the flank.

o.r: Now and then you get as far as the cross. Play goes through you too.
You want the pure central role. The coach agrees, reluctantly.

x_tz_winger_duel.d: On Sunday you face the best winger in the league. The coach asks how you want to play it.

o.r: Ninety minutes glued to him. You never push on, but he never gets the ball.
You attack, so he has to chase you. Risky, but you get more crosses in.

x_tz_wingback.d: With the new system the full-back becomes a wing-back: the whole flank is yours, up and down.

o.r: More crosses, more running, more fatigue. At full time you’re empty but decisive.

o.l: Ask to stay in a back four
o.r: In a back four you feel at home. Sharper, less tired.

x_tz_freekick_cross.d: The corner taker is injured. Your cross is the most accurate in the squad.

o.r: Corners and wide free kicks are yours. The headers are grateful.

o.l: Prefer the ball on the ground
o.r: You leave set pieces to others and work on one-on-ones.

x_tz_hamstring.d: A sprint to stop a counter and you feel your hamstring go. A month out and a little less burst.

x_tz_young_rival.t: The kid who runs twice as much
x_tz_young_rival.d: A nineteen-year-old full-back who never tires comes up from the academy. Your place isn’t safe any more.

o.r: You don’t outrun him, but you read play earlier. The coach won’t drop you.

o.rw: You match his pace all year. The place stays yours.
o.rl: He’s a decade younger. From January he starts.

x_med_tactical_fouls.d: The team concedes too many counters. The assistant explains when it pays to stop play with a foul.

o.r: A few more yellows, a few fewer counters. The coach approves.
You position yourself better and the counters never start.

x_med_distance_shots.d: Opponents always leave you free at the edge of the box: they think you never shoot.

o.rw: On the third chance you put it in the top corner. Since then someone always closes you down.
o.rl: Three shots into the stands. The coach asks you to go back to passing.

o.r: Free at the edge you see the whole pitch. Team-mates get better service.

x_med_double_pivot.d: They pair you with a technical midfielder. One of you has to do the running for both.

o.r: He plays, you recover. The team finds balance, your legs a bit less.
You learn to swap roles. You touch more balls and make fewer mistakes.

x_med_ban_appeal.d: Two bookings in ten minutes, the second for a shirt pull in midfield. The team holds on with ten, you watch from the tunnel.

x_med_libero_role.d: The coach suggests dropping between the centre-backs when the team builds play. Fewer kilometres, more responsibility.

o.r: From there you see everything and run half as much. Your career lengthens.
Your place is where the ball is won. For a while longer.

x_mez_trequartista.d: In a friendly you play as a number ten and make the difference. But there you’re little use when the other team has the ball.

o.r: More goals and assists. When it’s time to defend, someone grumbles.
The dirty work stays yours. The coach trusts you.

x_mez_box_to_box.d: GPS data says you run less than the other midfielders. The fitness coach offers a running programme.

o.r: A summer of intervals. Now you top the distance chart.
You play two-touch and the ball runs for you. The data stays the same, the play improves.

x_mez_dribble_school.d: A friend invites you to a five-a-side team during the break. Tight spaces, the ball always at your feet.

o.r: You come back with a first touch nobody had taught you.
You watch games and study passing lanes.

x_mez_last_minute.d: A late run to the far post, the ball arrives, a side-foot finish. A game that looked lost becomes yours.

x_mez_captain_kid.d: The club has bought an eighteen-year-old midfielder in your role and asks you to guide him.

o.r: You teach him timing. Watching him grow changes how you see the pitch.
You still have a lot to give. The kid will learn by watching.

x_ala_right_left.d: The coach says you can get twenty goals or twenty assists, but not both. You have to decide what player to be.

o.r: Every move ends with your shot. The goals come.
You reach the byline and deliver clean balls. The striker is grateful.

x_ala_press_winger.d: The new coach wants the winger to be the first defender: press the opposing full-back every time they build.

o.r: The coach loves you. You reach the box less fresh.
With the ball you’re devastating. Without it, they shout at you.

x_ala_speed_record.d: League data crowns you the fastest player of the season. Opposing full-backs take note.

x_ala_diving.d: A dive of yours in the box wins a penalty. VAR shows everything. The press accuses you, your fans defend you.

o.r: The row lasts weeks. Referees now watch you with suspicion.
A simple sentence at the press conference. The matter closes in a day.

x_ala_fullback_conversion.d: The burst isn’t what it was. The coach sees you as a wing-back, where the foot matters more than the legs.

o.r: The cross is still yours. You play with more time and more pitch ahead.
As long as you can beat your man, you stay where you hurt teams.

x_pun_partner.d: A prolific striker arrives. The team plays two up front and you have to work out who leads the line.

o.r: You stay in the box and he works for you. The good balls arrive.
You become the foil. Fewer goals for you, more for the team.

x_pun_headers.d: The assistant coach noticed you close your eyes when heading. He proposes a month with the ball machine.

o.r: A sore neck for weeks. Then you watch the ball all the way onto your head.
You leave crosses to others. You attack the space in behind.

x_pun_hat_trick_ball.d: Three goals in one half. The referee hands you the match ball and every team-mate signs it.

x_pun_offside_trap.d: In the last month you’ve been flagged offside fifteen times. The coach shows you the videos: you always go a moment early.

o.l: Work on the timing of your runs
o.r: You train watching the line, not the ball. Fewer goals ruled out.

o.l: Play more with your back to goal
o.r: Instead of running in behind, you come short. The team pushes up.

x_pun_goal_celebration.d: Fans ask you online to come up with a celebration of your own.

o.r: After your first goal every kid in town copies it.

o.l: Run to your team-mates, as always
o.r: The goal belongs to everyone. The fans like that too.

x_y_first_team_training.d: You’re called up to train with the senior squad twice a week. It’s another speed altogether.

o.r: You leave exhausted, but the coach noticed. Your strength improves.
You ask the veterans about what you lack. The gap closes slowly.

x_y_scholarship.d: An American university offers you a scholarship: football and a degree. Your club would rather you stayed.

o.r: You study at night with books on the team bus. A plan B in your pocket.
The club appreciates it. All your energy goes onto the pitch.

x_y_parents.d: Your father shouts instructions from the stands every game, contradicting the coach. Team-mates joke about it.

o.r: He’s your biggest fan. The coach is a little less happy.
An argument in the car, then he understands. On the pitch you only listen to the coach.

x_y_social_star.d: A training video of yours goes round the world. Agencies offer you sponsored content.

o.r: You become a famous face before a famous player. Sleep hours drop.
The video stays a nice memory. Your head stays on the ball.

x_y_growth_plate.d: Your body grows faster than your muscles. Three weeks out and a stretching programme for the whole year.

x_y_foreign_academy.d: A top foreign club offers your agent a place in its youth side. Your club promises you playing time.

o.r: At the end of the season your agent will look for the right club. The club knows.
The coach appreciates it and keeps an eye on you. You earn your place at home.

x_y_youth_cup.d: The youth team plays the European age-group tournament. They ask you to drop down from the first team for the finals.

o.rw: You’re the player of the tournament. Scouts take notes.
o.rl: Out in the quarter-finals. A nice experience, nothing more.

o.r: The coach appreciates the choice. He gives you a cup debut.

x_p_europe_night.d: European football and the league every three days. The coach lets you choose whether to play them all or manage yourself.

o.l: You want to play them all
o.rw: On cup nights you’re transformed. Europe starts to know your name.
o.rl: By February your legs have gone. You pay for it in the league.

o.r: You arrive fresh for the games that matter. The coach appreciates it.

x_p_abroad_language.d: At {club} everyone speaks a language you don’t know. The dressing room splits into little groups.

o.r: After three months you give interviews without a translator. Team-mates adopt you.
On the pitch you communicate with gestures. Off it you stay a little isolated.

x_p_relegation_fight.d: {club} are bottom of the table in January. A stronger team asks your agent about you.

o.r: You become the symbol of survival, whatever happens. Fans and coach won’t forget.

o.l: Ask to be sold in the summer
o.r: The club agrees to hear offers at the end of the season. The fans don’t.

x_p_big_club_bench.d: At {club} there are three internationals in your position. You play the minor cups and the last few minutes.

o.rw: Two perfect games when it matters and the coach makes you a starter.
o.rl: The three ahead don’t budge. You watch the big games from the bench.

o.r: At the end of the season you’ll look for a team to play for, then come back.
Your agent opens the market. The club isn’t pleased.

x_p_new_coach_system.d: The new manager asks you for tasks you’ve never done and warns: whoever doesn’t adapt doesn’t play.

o.r: Uncomfortable months, but you improve exactly where you were weakest. And you play.
You keep doing what you do best. The coach glares at you.

x_p_fan_protest.d: After four defeats fans wait for the team outside the training ground. They want to talk to someone.

o.l: Go out and talk to them
o.r: You listen and promise effort. The fans respect you, the club dislikes the initiative.
You stay out of it. Some people in the stands notice.

x_p_contract_bonus.d: Your new contract includes a bonus if you play at least thirty games. The doctor advises skipping a few.

o.r: You play through a few knocks. The bank balance smiles, the body less so.
The bonus may not come. Your body is grateful.

x_p_after_trophy.d: The trophy is still in the cabinet and the city hasn’t stopped celebrating. Pre-season starts in a week.

o.l: Enjoy the summer to the full
o.r: Parties, trips, interviews. You return happy and a few kilos heavier.
The hunger stays intact. The coach holds you up as an example.

x_p_after_relegation.d: The team has gone down. The president calls you: he wants to rebuild around you.

o.l: Stay to bring them back up
o.r: One division lower, but you’re the leader. The coach hands you the team.
You don’t want to lose a year. At the end of the season your agent will find a club.

x_p_after_injury.d: You’re available again, but the physio wants a month of gradual work before risking you for ninety minutes.

o.r: A few games missed, but the muscle comes back as before. Better, even.
The coach throws you in. You’re decisive, and a little more exposed.

x_p_teammate_depression.t: The team-mate who no longer laughs
x_p_teammate_depression.d: A team-mate misses training and doesn’t answer messages. Nobody knows what’s wrong.

o.l: Go to see him at home
o.r: You talk all evening. He asks for help. The dressing room pulls together around you.
The professionals handle it. You stay a little on the sidelines.

x_p_charity_match.d: In the summer break you’re invited to a match between legends and today’s stars to raise money.

o.r: You play alongside heroes you watched as a kid. The photos end up everywhere.
You send a signed shirt for the auction. Holidays stay holidays.

x_p_agent_switch.d: Football’s most powerful agent calls you. He promises a bigger club within a year.

o.r: Your name starts appearing in the papers. Offers will come at the end of the season.
You don’t need a rushed jump. The club appreciates the calm.

x_p_derby_week.d: The city talks about nothing else. A journalist asks you to send a message to the rivals.

o.rw: You win and the line becomes a chant. Your end adopts you.
o.rl: You lose. The line comes back at you for months.

o.r: You play the derby on the pitch. Nobody can throw anything back at you.

x_p_sleep_coach.d: The club hires a sleep expert. No phone after ten, cool room, fixed hours.

o.r: You wake up rested like you haven’t in years. You recover faster between games.
A few late TV series never killed anyone.

x_p_home_club_rival.d: The team your fans hate most wants you at any price. They pay double and play in the Champions League.

o.r: Fans burn your shirt. At the end of the season the market opens.
You become a symbol. Nobody can ever say anything to you.

x_p_fitness_app.d: During the holidays the club sends a personal programme to follow with an app. Nobody really checks.

o.r: You return to pre-season already fit. Sprint and stamina are grateful.
Ball, local pitch, friends. Your main strength stays sharp.

x_p_media_ban.d: After a controversial refereeing decision the club imposes a media blackout. A channel offers you an exclusive interview.

o.r: The club appreciates it. Journalists seek you out a little less.
The interview makes noise. Someone at the club doesn’t take it well.

x_v_last_contract_length.d: Your agent asks how you want to spend the years left: at your club, far away on a big contract, or wherever you play every week.

o.r: The dressing room and fans are home. The club knows.
At the end of the season your agent will hear the richest offers.
Even a division lower, as long as you play.

x_v_diet_change.d: A thirty-eight-year-old team-mate who still starts tells you his diet: no sugar, no alcohol, ten hours of sleep.

o.r: Three kilos lighter and the legs of five years ago. Dinners with friends a bit sad.
You enjoy life. Your body takes its course.

x_v_bench_leader.d: You play less than before. The coach asks you to be the voice of the dressing room even when you don’t come on.

o.r: You talk to the youngsters before games. When you come on, you already know what to do.

o.rw: Two starts played like a twenty-five-year-old. The place is yours again.
o.rl: The youngsters are quicker. Your outburst doesn’t change the pecking order.

x_v_farewell_national.d: The national coach calls to ask if you want to be part of the next cycle too. You have {caps} caps.

o.r: A low-key farewell. Your club gets back a player who no longer flies round the world.

o.l: You’re there as long as they want you
o.r: You don’t turn down the national shirt. The calendar gets heavy.

x_v_injury_scare.d: Your calf goes in a routine sprint. Three weeks out, and the feeling your body is sending you a message.

x_v_mentor_award.d: The youngster you mentored makes his international debut and says in an interview he owes it all to you.

x_v_press_retire_question.d: At every press conference the same question. Today even the president asks at dinner.

o.r: No date. Every game gets played as if it were normal.
You say it in front of everyone. From now on every stadium says goodbye.

x_n_club_vs_country.d: You have a muscle niggle. Your club wants to rest you over the break, the national coach wants you in camp anyway.

o.r: The coach appreciates it. You return to your club a little battered.
The club is grateful. Someone takes your national place for one break.

x_n_new_coach.d: The {nation} coach changes. At the first camp he explains a style nothing like your club’s.

o.r: You’re among the first to get it. He points you out to team-mates as an example.
On the pitch you do what you know. The coach takes note, not always kindly.

x_n_qualifier.d: A tough away game, a point needed to qualify. The coach asks if you feel up to starting.

o.rw: A perfect game, qualification secured. The papers put you on the cover.
o.rl: You struggle all game. The draw comes anyway, but not thanks to you.

o.r: Twenty minutes of order and control. The coach appreciates the humility.

x_n_debut_goal.t: First time with the national team
x_n_debut_goal.d: You come on in the eightieth minute of a friendly and touch your first balls in the {nation} shirt. Your whole family is in the stands.

x_n_captain_armband_day.d: The captain is suspended. The coach gives you the armband for the friendly: {caps} caps and the anthem sung in front of everyone.

x_i_derby_goal_banned.d: Because of chants from part of the stands, the team plays two home games behind closed doors. An empty stadium makes a strange noise.

x_i_coach_praise.d: At the press conference the coach says you’re the player he couldn’t do without. The line makes the front page.

x_i_youth_tournament_mvp.t: Best young player of the tournament
x_i_youth_tournament_mvp.d: At a summer tournament with teams from half of Europe you win best young player. Your agent gets three calls.

x_i_contract_dispute.d: The club has put off your renewal for months. Your agent loses patience and starts looking around.

x_i_club_crisis.d: The president is under investigation, sponsors flee, and in January the two best players leave. The team gets weaker.

x_i_signing_star.d: The club signs a star at the end of his career. He brings experience, goals and a queue of journalists to training.

x_i_team_bonding.d: A dinner organised by the senior players, phones in a basket at the door. From that evening the dressing room is different.

x_i_wrong_boots.d: An away game up north, frozen pitch, wrong studs. You slip for ninety minutes and ache everywhere the next day.

x_i_national_rumour.d: The national assistant coach is in the stands to watch you. Nobody calls, but the papers talk about it for a week.

x_i_goal_of_month.d: A volley from an impossible angle. The league picks it as goal of the month and every show airs it.

x_i_clean_sheet_run.d: Five clean sheets in a row. The papers talk about a wall and put your defence on the cover.
